title: Concentration and Extraction of Wastewater Samples
author: Catherine Pratt
materials: Add the following reagents to each required well of a row in the 96 Deep Well plate. Each sample requires one well in each row, for example 10 samples would take 10 wells in the row. Seal the plate after addition with parafilm or an adhesive plate seal to reduce evaporation. Row Reagents 1 A - 2 B 12 - Tip Comb 3 C - 4 D 1mL MagMAX Wash Buffer 5 E 1mL freshly prepared 80% Ethanol 6 F - 7 G - 8 H -

steps.title: Aliquot wastewater
steps.instruction: Using a serological pipette, transfer 35 mL of each wastewater sample into a labelled 50 mL Falcon tube.

steps.title: Mix and rest
steps.instruction: Invert the tube 5 times to mix, then let it sit for 45 seconds at room temperature (RT).

steps.title: Pre‑heat heat block
steps.instruction: Set a 1.5 mL tube heat block to 56 °C and allow it to reach temperature before the next step.

steps.title: Add Nanotrap ER1
steps.instruction: Add 100 µL of Nanotrap Enhancement Reagent 1 (ER1) to each sample tube.

steps.title: Mix and incubate
steps.instruction: Close the tube lids securely and invert 3–5 times to mix. Incubate at RT for 30 minutes, inverting 3 times every 5 minutes.

steps.title: First magnetic separation
steps.instruction: Place the tube on a 50 mL magnetic rack for 10 minutes or until the beads have separated from the solution.

steps.title: Discard supernatant (first)
steps.instruction: Using a serological pipette, carefully discard the supernatant without disturbing the bead pellet.

steps.title: Add Buffer 2 or water
steps.instruction: Add 1 mL of Nanotrap Buffer 2 **or** nuclease‑free water to the pellet, wetting the beads as the liquid is added.

steps.title: Resuspend beads
steps.instruction: Pipette to mix, or securely close the lid and swirl the tube to resuspend the beads. If beads stick to the wall, aspirate liquid from the bottom and gently dispense against the wall to wash them off.

steps.title: Transfer to 1.5 mL tube
steps.instruction: Using a 1 mL pipette, transfer the entire bead suspension into a labelled 1.5 mL tube, ensuring no liquid remains in the 50 mL tube.

steps.title: Second magnetic separation
steps.instruction: Place the 1.5 mL tubes on a 1.5 mL magnetic rack for 2 minutes or until the beads have separated from the solution.

steps.title: Discard supernatant (large volume)
steps.instruction: Using a 1 mL pipette, carefully discard the supernatant without disturbing the pellet.

steps.title: Discard residual supernatant
steps.instruction: Use a smaller pipette to remove the last of the supernatant, again avoiding disturbance of the pellet.

steps.title: Add MagMAX lysis buffer
steps.instruction: Remove the tubes from the magnet and add 500 µL of MagMAX Lysis Buffer (prepared with internal control if used) from the MagMAX Wastewater Ultra Nucleic Acid Isolation Kit. Pipette up and down until fully resuspended.

steps.title: Incubate with lysis buffer
steps.instruction: Close the lids securely, verify they are closed, and incubate the tubes on the 56 °C heat block for 10 minutes.

steps.title: Brief centrifugation
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the tubes for 3 seconds to collect any droplets.

steps.title: Third magnetic separation
steps.instruction: Place the tubes on a 1.5 mL magnetic rack for 2 minutes or until the beads have separated from the solution.

steps.title: Optional internal‑control spiking
steps.instruction: If using an internal control, prepare a mastermix for the number of samples + controls + 10 %: per sample add 500 µL MagMAX Wastewater Lysis Buffer and 2.5 µL internal‑control stock (10 000 copies/µL). Then add 525 µL Nanotrap Microbiome A particles to each sample, close lids, and invert 5 times to mix.

substeps.instruction: Add 400 µL nuclease‑free water to an empty well in row A to serve as the extraction control.
Transfer the prepared plate from the clean area to the biosafety cabinet.
Label one KingFisher 96‑Deep‑Well plate as “Sample Plate”.
Add 200 µL Lysis Buffer and 200 µL nuclease‑free water to one well of the Sample Plate to act as the extraction control.

steps.title: Choose extraction method – KingFisher Duo (manual, ≤12 samples)
steps.instruction: Proceed with the following steps if using the KingFisher Duo instrument.

substeps.instruction: Prepare 80 % ethanol: make 1.5 mL per sample/control (e.g., 12 × 1.5 mL = 18 mL total; mix 14.4 mL 100 % ethanol with 3.6 mL nuclease‑free water).

Prepare Binding Bead Mix for the number of samples + controls + 10 %: per sample add 20 µL MagMAX Binding Beads and 500 µL MagMAX Binding Buffer (total 520 µL). Invert 5–10 times, vortex beads before use, and do **not** pipette to mix.
Add 400 µL of the concentrated wastewater/lysis supernatant from the Ceres concentration step to row A of a 96‑well plate (one well per sample).
Check that the KingFisher Duo has the 12‑pin magnet, 12‑position heat block, and the ‘MagMAX_Wastewater_DUO96.bdz’ script installed.
Add 520 µL Binding Bead Mix to each sample (including extraction control) using a fresh tip per sample; do not pipette to mix, the instrument will mix. Invert if beads settle.
Add 40 µL Proteinase K to each sample (including extraction control); do not pipette to mix.
Run the ‘MagMAX_Wastewater_DUO96’ script on the KingFisher Duo, loading the plate and an elution strip when prompted.
After the run, add 100 µL MagMAX Elution Buffer to each tube in the elution strip, close the strip tubes, and remove lids before loading into the instrument.
At the end of the run, immediately remove the plate, seal it, and centrifuge if possible.

Aliquot the extracted nucleic acid into two 50 µL aliquots (one for PCR, stored at 4 °C overnight; one for sequencing, stored at –20 °C). If total volume is <100 µL, make a single 50 µL PCR aliquot and keep the remainder for sequencing.

steps.title: Choose extraction method – KingFisher Flex (automated, ≤96 samples)
steps.instruction: Proceed with the following steps if using the KingFisher Flex instrument.

substeps.instruction: Prepare 80 % ethanol: make 1.5 mL per sample/control (e.g., 96 × 1.5 mL = 144 mL total; mix 115.2 mL 100 % ethanol with 28.8 mL nuclease‑free water).

Prepare Binding Bead Mix for the number of samples + controls + 10 %: per sample add 20 µL MagMAX Binding Beads and 500 µL MagMAX Binding Buffer (total 520 µL). Invert 5–10 times, vortex beads before use, and do **not** pipette to mix.
Label three KingFisher 96‑Deep‑Well plates (Wash 1, Wash 2, Elution).
Add 1 mL MagMAX Wash Buffer to each well of Wash 1 plate.
Add 1 mL freshly prepared 80 % ethanol to each well of Wash 2 plate.
Add 100 µL MagMAX Elution Buffer to each well of the Elution plate. Seal all plates with parafilm or adhesive seal.
Add 400 µL of the supernatant from Ceres enrichment to the Sample plate (one well per sample).
Check that the KingFisher Flex has the 96‑pin magnet, 96‑position deep‑well heat block, and the ‘MagMAX_Wastewater_Flex96_V2.bdz’ script installed.
Add 520 µL Binding Bead Mix to each sample (including extraction control) using a fresh tip per sample; do not pipette to mix. Invert if beads settle.
Add 40 µL Proteinase K to each sample (including extraction control); do not pipette to mix.
Run the ‘MagMAX_Wastewater_Flex96_V2.bdz’ script on the KingFisher Flex, loading the four prepared plates and a fifth 96‑Deep‑Well plate containing the tip comb when instructed.
At the end of the run, centrifuge the plate if possible.
Aliquot the extracted nucleic acid into two 50 µL aliquots (PCR at 4 °C, sequencing at –20 °C) or a single 50 µL PCR aliquot if volume is insufficient.

steps.title: Manual bead‑based extraction (heat‑block)
steps.instruction: Proceed with the following steps if performing a fully manual extraction without a KingFisher instrument.

substeps.instruction: Label 1 × 1.5 mL tubes for each sample.
Add 520 µL Binding Bead Mix (20 µL beads + 500 µL buffer) to each tube; invert 5–10 times, vortex beads before use, and use a fresh tip per tube. Do not pipette to mix.
Add 40 µL Proteinase K to each tube; do not pipette to mix.
Close lids securely and vortex to mix.
Incubate on a heat block set at 65 °C for 5 minutes.
During this incubation, change the heat‑block temperature to 75 °C (pre‑heat for the next step).
Spin the tubes briefly in a micro‑centrifuge, then place on a 1.5 mL magnetic rack for at least 5 minutes or until beads separate.
Using a 1 mL pipette set to 1000 µL, discard all supernatant without touching the beads.
Remove tubes from the magnet and add 1 mL MagMAX Wash Buffer to each tube; pipette or vortex to resuspend beads.
Place tubes back on the magnetic rack for 3 minutes or until beads separate.
Using a 1 mL pipette set to 1000 µL, discard the wash supernatant.
Remove tubes from the magnet and add 1 mL freshly prepared 80 % ethanol; discard supernatant after 3 minutes on the rack as above.
Briefly centrifuge the tubes and return them to the magnetic rack.
Remove residual ethanol with a P20 pipette.
With lids open, air‑dry the beads on the magnetic stand for 2 minutes (do not exceed 2 minutes).
Add 100 µL MagMAX Elution Solution to each tube (add to all samples before moving on to avoid over‑drying).
Resuspend beads by pipetting.
Close lids securely and incubate on a heat block at 75 °C for 5 minutes.
Briefly centrifuge the tubes and place on the magnetic stand for 3 minutes or until beads separate.
Aliquot the supernatant (eluted nucleic acid) into two 50 µL aliquots (PCR at 4 °C, sequencing at –20 °C) or a single 50 µL PCR aliquot if volume is insufficient.
